q: In Fig. 8 (the SOT108-1 package outline drawing), across which features of the package is the dimension labeled HE measured?
options_raw: Across the outer extremities of the formed leads on the two lead-bearing sides (overall width including leads)
Across the two sides of the plastic body only, excluding the leads
Across the two ends of the package body in the long direction, spanning all 14 lead positions
From the seating plane up to the top surface of the package body
fact: In the end view at the upper right of the drawing, the HE arrow spans the full width from the outer edge of the left gull-wing lead foot to the outer edge of the right one, while the arrow labelled E directly above it stops at the plastic body sides.
why_arbitrary: Nothing in the letter HE says whether it includes the leads or only the body; only the extent of the drawn arrow relative to the body outline settles it.

q: In Figure 8-1, to which rail is the clamping diode that conducts the positive input clamp current (+IIK) at the logic input connected?
fact: In the schematic the diode labelled +IIK sits in the upper-left quadrant with its cathode on the horizontal wire that runs to the VCC terminal at the top of the dashed Device box; the -IIK diode below it goes to the GND wire.
why_arbitrary: The label +IIK alone does not say which rail the diode returns to; only tracing the drawn wire up to VCC rather than down to GND resolves it.

q: In the solder paste stencil design drawing for PW0014A, what are the length and width of each of the 14 stencil apertures?
fact: The callout 14X (1.5) at the top of the aperture array dimensions the horizontal extent of one aperture and 14X (0.45) on the left dimensions its vertical extent; 12X (0.65) below is the pitch, not an aperture size.
why_arbitrary: Which of the three loose numbers on the drawing belongs to the aperture rather than the pitch or the span is fixed only by where each dimension's arrows land.

q: In the land pattern example for PW0016A, what is the center-to-center pitch between adjacent pads?
fact: The callout 14X (0.65) on the left of the land pattern spans from one pad centerline to the next, giving the pad-to-pad pitch; 16X (0.45) and 16X (1.5) are the pad width and length, and (5.8) is the row-to-row span.
why_arbitrary: Four separate parenthesised numbers appear on the same drawing and only the placement of the 0.65 dimension between two pad centerlines identifies it as the pitch.

q: In the land pattern example for the X2SON package DPW0005A, what is the diameter of the via shown in the center thermal pad?
fact: The leader pointing at the small circle in the middle diamond-shaped pad is annotated (Ø 0.1) VIA, near the top center of the drawing.
why_arbitrary: The drawing also carries 0.05 MIN, (0.21) and (□ 0.25) callouts in the same neighbourhood, so only following the leader line to the circle picks out the via diameter.

q: In the TAPE AND REEL BOX DIMENSIONS drawing at the top of the page, which of the labeled edges (W, L, or H) is the one whose value is 35.0 mm for the SOT-23 (DBV) TL431 devices listed?
options_raw: H, the short vertical edge dimensioned on the right-hand side wall of the box
W, the long lower edge running down to the left of the box
L, the long lower edge running down to the right of the box
W, the short vertical edge dimensioned on the right-hand side wall of the box
fact: The isometric box pictogram carries W on the lower-left base edge, L on the lower-right base edge and H on the short vertical dimension at the right side wall; the table row for TL431ACDBVR (SOT-23, DBV) lists Height 35.0 mm against Length 210.0 and Width 185.0.
why_arbitrary: Which of the three drawn edges bears which letter is a property of this particular pictogram, not something derivable from the table alone.

q: In the land pattern example for the X2QFN package RUC0014A, what are the two dimensions of each of the 14 signal pads?
fact: At the upper left of the land pattern, 14X (0.6) dimensions the long side of one pad and 14X (0.2) its short side; 8X (0.4) and 2X (0.4) are pitches and (1.8), (1.6) are overall spans.
why_arbitrary: Several 0.4 and 1.8 callouts sit on the same drawing, so only the arrow extents distinguish the pad's own two dimensions from the pitches and spans.

q: In the TAPE AND REEL BOX DIMENSIONS drawing at the top of the page, which labeled edge (W, L, or H) corresponds to the 45.0 mm figure listed for TPA3116D2DADR?
options_raw: H, the short vertical edge dimensioned on the right-hand side wall of the box
L, the long lower edge running down to the right of the box
W, the long lower edge running down to the left of the box
L, the short vertical edge dimensioned on the right-hand side wall of the box
fact: The box pictogram labels the short vertical dimension at the right side wall H, the lower-left base edge W and the lower-right base edge L; the TPA3116D2DADR row lists Length 356.0, Width 356.0 and Height 45.0 mm.
why_arbitrary: Because Length and Width are both 356.0 for this device, only reading which drawn edge carries the H label ties 45.0 mm to a specific edge of the picture.

q: In Fig. 1 (the patient flow diagram), how many patients allocated to SDBP-B actually received the assigned bowel preparation?
fact: Following the right-hand branch of the flow diagram, the box 'Allocated to SDBP-B (n = 71)' leads down to 'Received assigned bowel prep (n = 63)', which in turn leads to 'Had BBPS score (n = 60)'.
why_arbitrary: Three arms each show a received-prep count (63, 60, 63) and a BBPS count (56, 58, 60), so only following the arrows down from the SDBP-B box picks the right number.

q: In the land pattern example for PW0024A, what is the length of each of the 24 pads?
fact: The callout 24X (1.5) at the top of the pad array spans the horizontal (long) extent of one pad; 24X (0.45) on the left is the pad width and 22X (0.65) the pitch.
why_arbitrary: The drawing carries 1.5, 0.45, 0.65 and 5.8 as bare parenthesised numbers, and only the direction and extent of each dimension arrow says which one is the pad length.

q: In the upper typical application schematic (IMON 3rd Order Thermal Compensation Application), between which pins of the AOZ23655QI is the thermistor network containing RNTC(T) connected?
options_raw: Between the IMON pin and analog ground (the AGND net)
Between the ISEN_P and ISEN_N pins
Between the LL pin and analog ground
Between the IMON pin and the LL pin
fact: In the upper schematic the IMON pin runs left to a node with C5, then down through RS into the RC / RS1+RNTC(T) ladder, whose bottom node ends in an analog-ground symbol; the LL pin has its own separate C6/RLL branch, and RNTC(T) only appears in the ISEN network in the lower (2nd order) schematic.
why_arbitrary: The same device is drawn twice on this page with RNTC(T) in a different place each time, so only tracing the wires of the upper schematic determines where the thermistor network hangs.

q: In Figure 2-3, between which two points on the CHIP_EN waveform is the interval tRST measured?
options_raw: From where the falling CHIP_EN crosses VIL_nRST to where the rising CHIP_EN crosses VIL_nRST again
From where CHIP_EN first begins to fall from its high level to where it returns to its full high level
From where the power rails reach 2.8 V to where CHIP_EN first crosses VIL_nRST
Between the two points where CHIP_EN crosses the 2.8 V level
fact: The tRST arrow at the top right of the timing diagram is bounded by two dashed verticals that drop onto the CHIP_EN trace exactly where it crosses the VIL_nRST dashed horizontal on the way down and on the way back up.
why_arbitrary: CHIP_EN's dip has several candidate landmarks (start of fall, flat bottom, full recovery) and only the drawn dashed verticals show which pair the arrow spans.
